purpose: This table provides one cleaned row per scheduled NYC departure (JFK, LGA, EWR) for January-June 2013, covering flight identifiers, scheduled and actual departure/arrival times, delays, and route/distance details, feeding downstream on-time-performance and route analysis.
usage: Read dep_time, dep_delay, arr_time, arr_delay, air_time, and tailnum as nullable fields: a null in these columns means the flight never departed or its arrival/duration was not recorded, not a data quality failure, so consumers must filter or handle these nulls deliberately rather than treating them as errors. Join on carrier and flight with the date and sched_dep_time grain to identify a scheduled flight instance.
limitations: Airbyte capture metadata (_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, _airbyte_meta) was dropped as non-business data. dep_time, dep_delay, arr_time, arr_delay, and air_time carry null rates between 2.9% and 3.3%, and tailnum carries a 0.9% null rate; these are retained as nulls per business meaning but mean roughly 3% of rows are incomplete for delay and duration analysis. No duplicate rows were found (duplicate_row_rate 0.0), so no dedupe logic was applied, but the declared grain has not been measured against the full warehouse and should be validated before approval.
